newsitem.title: BURUNDI: Burundi army says rebels kill five civilians.
newsitem.headline: Burundi army says rebels kill five civilians.

text.p: The Burundian army said on Wednesday Hutu rebels killed five civilians near the capital Bujumbura and residents in revenge killed one rebel on Tuesday night.

Commandant Celestin Ntahomvukiye told the independent radio production house Studio Ijambo the rebels attacked Buhanda hill in the Bujumbura area, killing five Hutu civilians and wounding five others.
"The rebels attacked people in that place because they accused them of collaborating with the Burundian military," said Ntahomvukiye, who added that residents captured one rebel and killed him.
Studio Ijambo on Tuesday quoted residents of the northwest provinces of Cibitoke and Bubanza as saying more than 600 Hutu civilians had been killed by rival Hutu rebels since mid-July.

The residents, who had since fled, said the civilians were killed in fighting between the Hutu National Liberation Front (FNL) and the Forces for the Defence of Democracy, the armed wing of CNDD led by former interior minister Leonard Nyangoma.

They said the FNL accused the FDD of collaborating with Burundi's Tutsi military ruler Pierre Buyoya because the CNDD had agreed to peace talks with his military government, which seized power a year ago.
More than 250,000 people have been killed in massacres and civil war between the Tutsi-dominated army and Hutu rebels since the assassination of Burundi's first Hutu president in October 1993.
